text: Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, told Ahab: As surely as the LORD, Israel's God, lives — the one I serve — there will be no dew or rain in these years except by my word.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:
Leave this place, go east, and hide by the brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.
You will drink from the brook, and I have ordered ravens to feed you there.
So Elijah did as the LORD told him and settled by the brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.
After some time the brook dried up, since no rain had fallen anywhere in the land.
Then the word of the LORD came to him:
Get up and go to Zarephath, near Sidon, and stay there — I have directed a widow there to feed you.
So he went to Zarephath. At the town gate he found a widow gathering sticks; he called to her and asked for a little water to drink.
As she went to get it, he called out asking her to also bring him a piece of bread.

She answered, As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread — only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug; I am gathering sticks to cook one last meal for myself and my son before we die.
Elijah told her, Don't be afraid; go and do as you planned, but first make me a small loaf from what you have and bring it to me, then make something for yourself and your son.
For this is what the LORD, Israel's God, says: the jar of flour will not run out and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain on the land.
She went and did as Elijah told her, and she and her household ate for many days.
The jar of flour did not run out and the jug of oil did not run dry, exactly as the LORD had promised through Elijah.
Some time later the woman's son became sick, and his illness grew worse until he stopped breathing.
She said to Elijah, What do you have against me, man of God? Have you come to remind me of my sin and kill my son?
He said, Give me your son, took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
Then he cried out to the LORD: my God, have you brought tragedy even on this widow I am staying with, by killing her son?
He stretched himself over the boy three times and cried out, LORD my God, let this boy's life return to him.
The LORD listened to Elijah's cry, and the boy's life returned to him and he lived.
Elijah brought the boy down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother, saying, Look, your son is alive.
The woman said to Elijah, Now I know for certain that you are a man of God and that the LORD's word in your mouth is true.
